rows.source_review: In the unchanged HBase 2.6.6 TestRegionMove.testDisableAndMove JUnit, both move calls intentionally throw B2 DoNotRetryRegionException. For the response-loss candidate, the first UnassignRegion RPC reached AssignmentManager with an OPEN region and no procedure, completed CloseRegionProcedure and UNASSIGN TransitRegionStateProcedure, and persisted CLOSED in hbase:meta before the successful RPC response was replaced by a SocketTimeoutException. HBaseAdmin rebuilt the same region-only UnassignRegion request in RpcRetryingCallerImpl; Master.proto has no operation nonce. The retry reached B2 with CLOSED and no procedure, so the server correctly rejected a duplicate unassign and the original JUnit failed at admin.unassign. Two clean exact-selector replays (49.18 s and 46.41 s) reproduced this ordering and JUnit found=1 succeeded=0 failed=1; an assign-response replay (50.19 s) showed symmetric OPEN after completed assign. Admin.assign/unassign Javadocs explicitly allow IOException for remote or network exceptions. A lost response therefore leaves client completion ambiguous, and no stronger contract violation or internal invariant breach is established. The client-level observation remains candidate_unconfirmed, not a confirmed new bug.

rows.source_review: The original test holds FSNamesystem.readLock around Saver.save (TestFSImageWithSnapshot.java:143-155). Snapshot creation changes SnapshotManager.numSnapshots under FSNamesystem.writeLock (FSNamesystem.java:7175-7192). Saver serializes the in-memory snapshot list and compares its count with that manager count (FSImageFormatPBSnapshot.java:435-468). A checked IOException at writeDelimitedTo aborts serialization before the guard; heartbeat/RPC faults do not modify the locked snapshot count. The selected equality was true in every fault-retaining trace.
